title: Understanding the human brain: New frontiers in neurology
summary: Discover how technology is transforming neuroscience and supporting earlier diagnosis and more personalised treatments of neurological conditions.
body_text: Understanding the human brain: New frontiers in neurology 9 July 2026 Alina Lobacheva, Sustainable Portfolio Manager Share page via Facebook Share page via X Share page via LinkedIn Share page via email Please note: This article is designed to be thought leadership content to offer big picture views and analysis of interesting issues and trends that matter to our clients (1) . It is not designed to be taken as preferred view from Barclays Private Bank and Wealth Management, expert advice, investment advice or a recommendation and any reference to specific companies is therefore not an opinion as to their present or future value or broader credentials (climate, sustainability or otherwise). Reliance upon any of the information in this article is at the sole discretion of the reader. Some of the views and issues discussed in this article may derive from third-party research or data which is relied upon by Barclays Private Bank and Wealth Management and may not have been validated. Such research and data are made available as additional information for the reader where appropriate. “The brain, the masterpiece of creation, is almost unknown to us.” – Nicolaus Steno, 1669 For most of human history, the brain has largely remained a black box. Paul Broca identified a region of the brain responsible for speech in 1861, and scientists began mapping broad cortical areas after Korbinian Brodmann published his landmark cortical atlas in 1909. Major breakthroughs came with the advent of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in the 1970s and functional MRI (fMRI) in the early 1990s. These technologies allowed researchers to directly observe large-scale patterns of brain activity. Monumental international efforts, such as the Human Connectome Project, used MRI to map large-scale human brain networks, but the detailed underlying circuitry and molecular interactions remained largely hidden. The human brain is an incredibly complex network of over 80 billion neurons, trillions of synapses and an entire ecosystem of supporting structures. Until a few years ago, mapping just 1mm³ of the human brain was impossible due to the sheer amount of data that would need to be analysed and processed. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) and broader advancements in technology, as well as electron microscopy, are making detailed brain mapping a reality, leading to exciting opportunities and advancements in neuroscience. “The connectome is the beginning of the digital transformation of brain science” – Professor H. Sebastian Seung (Princeton University) Mapping the brain Neural networks Our brain makes us who we are, serving as the biological foundation of cognition, personality, emotion, and behaviour. Complex, distributed interactions between neurons give rise to our thoughts, memories, and actions. When the connectivity of neural networks is altered, brain function is affected. Modern neurology uses the term connectopathies to describe conditions believed to be rooted in the atypical wiring of the brain’s neural networks. Advancements in AI, electron microscopy, and large‑scale data integration are enabling researchers to map brain circuits in organisms ranging from fruit flies to mammals (2) . These maps could become the foundation for understanding a range of conditions, such as dementia (3) and schizophrenia (4) , assisting with early detection and, over time, developing more targeted treatments. In 2024, an international collaboration called FlyWire published their research on the first full connectome (map of neural connections within the brain) of an adult fruit fly (5) . Scientists mapped over 50 million connections across nearly 140,000 neurons (6) . Just one year later, in 2025, the MICrONS (Machine Intelligence from Cortical Networks) consortium (7) published a precise map of the vision centres of a mouse brain. Covering more than half a billion connections across 1mm³ of brain tissue (8) , this tiny sample is about 20 times bigger than the complete fruit fly brain and more complex (9) , showcasing the massive leaps in research capabilities. Researchers used AI to trace every contour of every neuron, and the output was proofread by humans. The project created 1.6 petabytes of data, equivalent to storing 320,000 HD movies. Creating a map like this seemed impossible just a few decades ago, but a combination of new scientific techniques and advancements in technology have “opened the door to a new era of realistic brain simulations” (10) . The dataset is publicly available and has already led to interesting discoveries (11) . While creating a full human brain connectome will take massive computational resources, years of coordinated neuroscience research and further advancements in imaging, automation, and data analysis, recent breakthroughs act as a proof-of-concept. In 2021, Google Research released the H01 database, in collaboration with the Lichtman Laboratory at Harvard University. The database includes imaging data that covers roughly 1mm³ of the human cerebral cortex, and includes tens of thousands of reconstructed neurons, millions of neuron fragments, 130 million annotated synapses and 104 proofread cells (12) . H01 remains the largest and most detailed synapse-level reconstruction of human brain tissue and the first large‑scale study of synaptic connectivity. Connectomics can be revolutionary in helping us understand neural circuit function and revealing altered patterns of connectivity that may support the early diagnosis of neurological conditions. However, it does not explain why specific neurons behave differently or undergo progressive functional decline. To add these critical pieces to the puzzle, understanding cell biology is equally important. “If you want to understand function, study structure.” – Francis Crick Cell function Inside every brain cell, there are tiny components that determine how that cell behaves – proteins, ions, neurotransmitters, and gene-regulating and signalling molecules. Some neurological disorders, such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s, may be driven by changes in protein structure or by faulty interactions between proteins and other molecules inside the cell. Proteins are made from long chains of amino acids, each with a unique complex 3D structure. Understanding just one structure used to take years of slow and expensive lab work costing hundreds of thousands of dollars. In 2020, Google’s DeepMind released AlphaFold 2, which was able to predict single protein structures with near-experimental accuracy in minutes, outperforming the next best system by a wide margin (13) . So far, AlphaFold has predicted over 200 million protein structures (nearly all catalogued proteins known to science). In 2024, John Jumper and Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind) received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing this AI-based tool (14) . The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database is freely available and over 2 million researchers in over 190 countries use it to inform their work (15) . AlphaFold 3, released in 2024, predicts not only the shape of a single protein, but how these interact with other essential biological components, such as DNA, RNA, drug‑like molecules, and ions. This has major implications for our understanding of neurological conditions and can accelerate drug discovery by shortening parts of the process from years to just a few months. Early detection and diagnostics Neurological conditions are a leading cause of ill health and disability worldwide, affecting more than 40% of the global population (16) . Some of these conditions can be prevented or treated, and early diagnosis can be critical to improved patient outcomes. Early neurological symptoms are often subtle and non‑specific, but AI models can detect weak, multivariate patterns in imaging and bio-signals that humans may struggle to recognise (17) . Across a range of neurological conditions, AI systems have demonstrated performance that matches or, in specific tasks, exceeds that of human experts (18) . For example, studies show that AI models analysing MRI scans can identify Alzheimer’s disease with accuracies exceeding 90%, in some cases detecting structural brain changes years before clinical symptoms become apparent (19) . AI tools can also analyse brainwave recordings (EEG (20) data) to help anticipate seizures, achieving prediction accuracies above 85%. Similarly, speech and movement-based models can identify early changes linked to Parkinson’s disease (21) . AI-based MRI image analysis has shown great promise when it comes to monitoring MS (multiple sclerosis) lesion activity. Research shows AI correctly detected new or enlarging lesions, key indicators of disease progression, in approximately 9 out of 10 cases, compared with around 6 out of 10 using routine radiology reports (22) . AI systems have also demonstrated their effectiveness in identifying early signs of ischemic stroke, detecting blocked brain blood vessels in around 94% of cases, compared with about 82% using standard scans alone (23) . Hospitals in the US (24) and the UK (25) are already using AI to help flag early signs of disease. Understanding the risks While AI tools can enhance our understanding of the human brain, they should supplement, rather than replace, a comprehensive medical assessment performed by an experienced physician. AI models can underperform and provide erroneous outputs for populations that were underrepresented during model training, resulting in delayed or incorrect treatment protocols. A number of lawsuits are also under way in relation to the denial of insurance claims as a result of AI-based claims analysis. In addition, overreliance on AI could contribute to skill degradation over time, resulting in a generation of physicians who are less proficient at performing assessments and interpreting results independently, and therefore less able to verify or challenge AI-based outputs. Data privacy and data integrity are key considerations. Large-scale brain mapping is complex and error prone. At the same time, AI models can generate realistic but fabricated data, and databases can become corrupted, either through deliberate manipulation or unintended model “hallucinations”, which would lead to misdiagnoses. Health-related data is personal and incredibly sensitive, carrying far greater implications than most other categories of information. Breaches of medical data can have profound consequences – from discrimination and financial harm to long-term psychological distress. As AI becomes more deeply integrated into diagnostics, personalised care, and large-scale brain-mapping initiatives, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and responsible use of health data is essential. Looking ahead Technology is reshaping our understanding of what is scientifically and clinically possible. In the decades ahead, sophisticated AI systems have the potential to move us closer to identifying the causes of a variety of neurological conditions and potentially developing personalised treatments. Multi-modal AI systems are already combining different types of information, from brain scans to speech and movement data, to provide a more comprehensive picture of brain function (26) . Digital brain twins are being developed to simulate disease progression, test interventions, and optimise therapies before they are applied in the real world (27) . Neuro‑adaptive therapies, which adjust to a patient’s brain activity in real time, are already used to help manage Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, and chronic pain, with wider applications across psychiatry and rehabilitation still under development (28) . Progress is never without risk, however, and early benefits are often not uniformly distributed or accessible. Data integrity, privacy, model bias, and the risk of overreliance all underscore the need for strong governance and human oversight. As we continue to push the boundaries of brain science, progress must be paired with safeguards to ensure technologies are deployed ethically, transparently, and in ways that strengthen, rather than compromise, patient care. title: The role of Delaware statutory trust services in an asset-backed securitization deal
summary: Here's an overview of how Delaware statutory trust services from UMB fit into an asset-backed security transaction.
body_text: In a previous post, we laid out a hypothetical asset-backed security (ABS) structure, a widget loan securitization, and outlined how UMB’s role as indenture trustee fits into the deal overall. Now, we’ll touch on the other main trustee role in a typical ABS structure: that of underlying (or owner) trustee and the closely related Delaware trustee services. In our widget securitization example, a non-bank lender works with an underwriter to determine a pool of loans to securitize. Then, the underwriter brings the newly created securities to market. Investors (noteholders) purchase interest in the securities and receive payments as borrowers repay their loans. Why Delaware statutory trust? The underlying trustee function is to hold the loans on behalf of the securities owners. Securitizations are often conducted under Delaware law, which requires an owner entity to make certain representations and warranties about the loans. To do so means the owner must be a Delaware statutory trust—that is, a trust registered in Delaware and created according to its long-established business law. My colleague, Kristin Moore, has worked in Delaware her entire career. She is president of UMB Delaware Inc., our office in Wilmington, Delaware, where we are registered with the state to provide Delaware statutory trust services. Therefore, we can work directly with underwriters and lenders to create the necessary special purpose vehicle (the trust) to own the loans, make representations and warranties required in a securitization and provide transfer and paying agent services on the certificates. Owner trustee services In addition to creating the trust, UMB can serve as its trustee—this is now the underlying/owner trustee function. As a federally regulated bank, UMB Bank, n.a. is exempt from local and state jurisdictional requirements. That’s essential in a securitization deal because registering in cities and counties across the country is impractical. Therefore, only a federally regulated bank—and one that meets capital requirements—can effectively serve as underlying trustee. Investors rely on the fact that the assets—that is, the securitized loans—are segregated (via the trust) from all other assets of the issuer/originator. The assets do not belong to UMB. Rather, UMB, serving as trustee, holds them on behalf of the noteholders who purchase securities. The owner trustee undertakes to perform such duties, and only such duties, as are specifically set forth in the trust agreement and the other transaction documents. That includes administration of the trust in the interest of the security holders. Broader context Our work as underlying trustee is part of a menu-of-services approach. The following list outlines other trust and agency services commonly needed in an ABS transaction. Indenture trustee – Ensure transactions are processed correctly and noteholders receive payments on the due dates, enforces representations and warranties, etc. Owner trustee services – Hold title to loans, process waterfall payments, etc. DTC settlement agent – S ettles the notes on behalf of a placement agent with DTC Collateral agent – Safeguards and processes borrower’s funds held as collateral Escrow agent – Safeguards and processes funds held in escrow until a closing occurs Verification agent – Verifies certain items on an electronic loan file Document custody – Holds custody of an electronic loan file Paying agent and registrar – Pays the investors or lenders (paying agent) and holds a list of the investors or lenders (registrar) Account bank – Opens and holds the trust account on behalf of the borrower Cash management – Moves the funds received and investing the funds on behalf of the borrower Calculation and tax agent – If needed, prepares the waterfall on behalf of the servicer Backup servicer – If needed, recalculates the servicer report and is prepared to step in for the primary servicer if needed Learn more about our specialty trust and agency solutions , including a full-range of trust services, escrow and agency assignments for large-scale and uniquely-structured transportation, infrastructure, real estate, ABS and other structured-financing projects.

title: How to Recognize Generative AI in Financial Fraud
summary: Updates, insights, and stories to feed your financial growth and showcase client success.
body_text: How to Recognize Generative AI in Financial Fraud Financial Well-Being Unless you live under a metaphorical rock, you’ve likely heard an increase in the use of terms like “AI,” “Chat GPT,” and “gen AI” over the last year. The artificial intelligence boom is in full swing. From businesses exploring how it can supercharge their workforce to individuals using it to ease the burden of everyday tasks, it has quickly become interwoven in so many facets of life – and has left us with questions and concerns. When it comes to the use of generative AI, criminals are no exception, using these tools to facilitate their scams and create synthetic content that can be very convincing. While the Southern First team is always working hard behind the scenes to protect your assets, we also want to make you aware of these tactics so you can protect yourself. Here are a few examples of content criminals are using AI to create to make their fraud schemes believable. Images: Realistic images for fictitious social media profiles Fraudulent identification documents such as driver’s licenses or credentials Photos to share with a victim in private communications to convince the victim they are speaking to a real person Images of celebrities or social media influencers promoting counterfeit products Images of natural disasters to elicit donations to fraudulent charities Pornographic images of a victim to demand payment in sextortion schemes Audio: Short audio clips containing a loved one’s voice in a crisis demanding financial assistance or a ransom Videos: Videos for real-time video chats with alleged company executives, law enforcement, or other authority figures Videos for private communications to “prove” they are a real person Fictitious or misleading promotional materials for investment fraud schemes How to protect yourself: Create a secret word or phrase with your family to verify their identity. Look for subtle imperfections in images and videos such as distortions, irregular faces, inaccurate shadows, lag time, watermarks, and unrealistic movements. Listen closely to the tone and word choice to distinguish a real voice from vocal cloning. Verify the identity of the person calling you by hanging up the phone, researching the contact, and calling their number directly. Never share sensitive information with people you have never met in person. Do not send money, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or other assets to people you have only met online or over the phone. If you have fallen victim to a financial fraud scheme, report it to your banker immediately. title: What Today's Teachers Want From the Hiring Process — And What It Means for Your District
summary: Today's teaching candidates expect hiring to move fast. Slow, bureaucratic processes cost districts their best candidates. Learn what the new generation of educators wants from the hiring experience, and how a principal-first approach can help your district move faster and hire for fit.
body_text: The K-12 hiring market has changed a lot in the last 20 years — and the rules your district is playing by may not match the game being played today. Here's the situation: according to the Institute of Education Sciences , an estimated 1 in 8 teaching positions is either unfilled or filled by a teacher not fully certified for their assignment. Meanwhile, 64% of schools report a lack of qualified candidates, and 62% say too few candidates are applying at all. The pipeline is genuinely thinner. And the teachers who are looking for jobs — predominantly Millennials and Gen Z — bring a different set of expectations to the search than the generations before them. If your hiring process hasn't kept pace, you're not just moving slowly. You're actively losing candidates to districts that have. The New Generation of Teachers Isn't Waiting Around The largest share of today's teaching workforce is made up of Millennials, with Gen Z steadily growing. Both of these generations have a fundamentally different relationship with job searching than their predecessors did. They research employers before applying. They want to understand a school's culture before committing to a lengthy application. And they expect the process to move. Today's job seekers expect hiring to move fast — and when it doesn't, they move on. Slow, bureaucratic processes significantly increase the risk of losing strong candidates mid-search, particularly among Gen Z, who have little patience for drawn-out timelines. The most common reason candidates drop out isn't compensation or role fit — it's receiving a competing offer while waiting for the process to finish. It's a reminder that in a competitive market, the most in-demand candidates have options — and they're exercising them. A Long Application Process Can Work Against You Most traditional district hiring flows look something like this: a job gets posted, candidates submit a full application (often 20–30 minutes or more of forms and uploads), someone reviews the pool, passes finalists to the principal, and then — weeks later — interviews begin. From a candidate's perspective, they've invested significant time with no signal of mutual interest, and often no real sense of whether this school is even the right fit for them. The effect of this is clear: applications that take more than 15 minutes to complete lose roughly two-thirds of candidates before they finish. And when candidates feel like they're just taking a number in a long line, they turn around and leave. The candidates most likely to leave mid-process are, by definition, your most in-demand ones — the teachers with options. Fit Isn't a Nice-to-Have. It Drives Retention. Here's what makes this especially costly for districts: filling a seat and filling it well are two very different outcomes. Research on teacher hiring has found that processes offering minimal interaction — beyond a single application and interview — prevent candidates from assessing their fit with the school, leading to misaligned placements, higher turnover, and lower job satisfaction. Teachers who experience a realistic preview of the job report greater satisfaction and are more likely to stay. In other words: the faster you can create a real, human connection between a teacher and a school, the better your odds of not just filling the role, but keeping that person in it. A Different Approach: Principal-First Matching This is exactly the problem Nimble Connect was designed to solve. Rather than asking teachers to submit a full application and wait, Connect works upstream of the formal application process entirely. Every week, principals receive a curated set of pre-screened, credentialed teacher profiles matched to their school's open roles and location — including teachers who may not have come across your district yet, or who are exploring their options but haven't committed to applying anywhere. Principals review them in 5–10 minutes — the interface is built around a simple yes/no review flow, similar in structure to the matching apps today's job seekers are already familiar with — and when there's mutual interest, we make the connection. Think of it as a chance to get your schools in front of a highly relevant audience and let principals make their pitch before candidates have narrowed their search. The formal application comes later, once there's already a relationship and a reason to commit. This matters because today's teachers — especially the most sought-after ones — want to know they're not just submitting into a void. They want to connect with a principal, understand the school's culture, and make an informed decision. That's not a generational quirk to work around. It's the signal of a teacher who cares about where they land. We hear occasionally from hiring teams who prefer to review candidates before they reach principals — which is a reasonable instinct rooted in years of established process. But here's the thing: all Connect candidates are pre-screened by Nimble for valid state credentials and eligibility to work in the US before they ever appear in a principal's queue. The vetting has already happened. What Connect does is bring qualified, interested teachers to the table faster , before they've accepted an offer from another district. In a market where 74% of districts struggled to fill open positions last year, protecting your process at the cost of your pipeline isn't a neutral tradeoff. The districts that will win the best teachers are the ones that can move quickly, make a genuine connection, and give candidates a real sense of what it's like to work in their schools. Ready to see how Nimble Connect works? It's designed around the hiring experience today's teachers expect — and it's helped districts not just fill vacancies, but fill them with candidates who are the right fit and stay. title: Poshmark Crosslisting: How Does it Work? All There is to Know
summary: Discover how Poshmark crosslisting can boost your sales by reaching more buyers across multiple marketplaces. Learn manual vs. automated methods.
body_text: Poshmark crosslisting is the process of taking an active listing from your Poshmark closet and publishing it on additional marketplaces like eBay, Mercari, and Depop so the same item reaches millions of additional potential buyers. Instead of depending on one marketplace's search algorithm or buyer traffic, crosslisting allows every listing to work harder. A dress sitting unsold on Poshmark may sell within hours on eBay. Since every marketplace has a unique user base, crosslisting helps sellers increase visibility without sourcing additional inventory. Sellers typically crosslist either by manually copying every listing to each marketplace or by using dedicated crosslisting software that does it for them. TL;DR Poshmark crosslisting duplicates existing listings onto additional marketplaces to reach more buyers. Sellers can crosslist manually or automate the process with specialized software. Crosslisting tools dramatically reduce listing time by importing inventory in bulk. Each marketplace requires listing adjustments to maximize search visibility and buyer engagement. Inventory synchronization helps prevent costly double sales across multiple platforms. Crosslisting creates a more stable resale business by reducing dependence on a single marketplace. The Basics: Manual vs. Automated Workflows There are two primary ways to crosslist a Poshmark closet . Understanding the daily workflow behind each method helps sellers determine which option makes the most sense for their business. Manual Crosslisting Manual crosslisting costs nothing beyond your time, making it an attractive option for beginners with a small inventory. Every listing, however, must be recreated individually on each marketplace. A typical workflow looks like this: Download the original high-resolution listing photos from Poshmar (do not screenshot). Open the destination marketplace in a separate browser tab. Create a new listing Upload the photos and videos Copy and paste the title Copy and paste the description Enter the category Select the correct size Add the brand Choose the appropriate color(s) Complete any required item specifics Enter the price. Publish the listing. Repeat the process for every marketplace. This process works reasonably well for sellers with only a handful of listings. Once a closet exceeds roughly 50 active items, however, manual crosslisting becomes a significant bottleneck. Updating listings, correcting mistakes, changing prices, and relisting stale inventory can consume hours every week. Don’t spend hours manually crosslisting. List to 10+ marketplaces in seconds with Vendoo Automated Crosslisting Crosslisting software fundamentally changes the workflow by eliminating most of the repetitive data entry. Instead of recreating every listing manually, sellers generally follow this process: Connect their Poshmark account to the software. Bulk import active listings. Review imported inventory inside one dashboard. Select one or multiple marketplaces. Publish listings simultaneously. Review any marketplace-specific fields before submitting. Modern crosslisting applications automatically map listing information to each marketplace's required form. Titles, descriptions, pricing, categories, photos, brands, and other listing details are transferred automatically, significantly reducing the amount of manual work required. Instead of spending several minutes recreating every listing, sellers can often publish dozens of listings during the same amount of time. I imported these shorts from Poshmark, then crosslisted to multiple marketplaces in just a few clicks! The Inventory Tracking Challenge The biggest challenge of crosslisting is inventory management . Because most resale items are one-of-a-kind, selling the same item twice creates a serious problem. If an item sells on Poshmark but remains active on another marketplace, another customer may purchase inventory that no longer exists. Sellers are punished for cancellations, plus it’s just poor customer service. Manual sellers typically manage this process by maintaining a spreadsheet that tracks every listing across every marketplace . Whenever something sells, they must immediately locate and delete the duplicate listings manually. This approach requires constant attention and becomes increasingly difficult as inventory expands. No one has time for that. Automated crosslisting software addresses this problem through inventory synchronization. When a connected marketplace reports a sale, compatible software automatically removes the listing from the seller's other marketplaces, greatly reducing the risk of accidental double sales. Key Marketplace Differences to Navigate Successful crosslisting involves much more than copying and pasting the same listing everywhere. Every marketplace has its own search algorithm, buyer expectations, listing requirements, and shopping culture. Adapting listings for each marketplace often produces better visibility and stronger conversion rates. eBay (Search-Driven) Poshmark encourages discovery through its social marketplace, where sharing listings and engaging with buyers can increase visibility. eBay operates very differently . Its search engine rewards descriptive, keyword-rich titles and complete Item Specifics. Sellers should optimize titles with relevant search phrases while completing fields such as: Material Pattern Style Sleeve Length Occasion Department Size Type Exact measurements when applicable These Item Specifics help eBay understand exactly what is being sold, making listings easier for buyers to find through search. Don’t skip them! The most common mistake that Poshmark sellers make when crosslisting to eBay is skipping the Item Specific Fields. 💡 Tip: Your item description is not “searchable” on eBay, meaning the words in the description do not yield in the buyer’s search. Mercari (Casual Shoppers and Competative Pricing) Mercari has a more casual marketplace than Poshmark, and buyers often expect competitive pricing. Many shoppers browse Mercari looking for everyday deals rather than curated closets or boutique-style listings. Mercari has a buyer fee, which is important to keep in mind when pricing . Because seller fees are generally lower, many resellers choose to price items slightly lower on Mercari while still earning a similar profit. This can make listings more attractive to buyers without significantly affecting your bottom line. Rather than using identical pricing across every marketplace, consider adjusting your Mercari prices to match buyer expectations and remain competitive. 💡 Tip: Mercari allows up to five hashtags! Be sure to add these as they help with searchability. Depop (Visuals & Audience) Depop attracts a younger audience that shops heavily based on trends, aesthetics, and visual presentation. Listings generally perform best when they feature: Bright, eye-catching photography Shorter descriptions Trend-focused keywords Popular aesthetic hashtags Measurements References to styles such as Y2K, vintage, cottagecore, gorpcore, grunge, or coquette when appropriate Unlike eBay, lengthy descriptions are typically less important . Buyers often respond more strongly to attractive images and concise descriptions with style words that quickly communicate the style and aesthetic of an item. 💡 Tip: Do not skip the style, attribute, and occasion dropdowns on Depop. They’re vital for your listing. Scaling Your Business with Multi-Platform Automation Crosslisting is valuable for any reseller, but automation becomes essential as inventory grows. Managing hundreds of listings across multiple marketplaces without software quickly becomes difficult. Instead of treating Poshmark as your primary inventory database, a centralized platform allows you to manage your entire business in one location. Centralized Inventory Management As your business scales, keeping inventory organized becomes just as important as creating listings. Vendoo serves as a centralized inventory hub where sellers can draft, edit, organize, and store their listings before publishing them to connected marketplaces. Instead of making updates separately on every platform, sellers maintain a single master listing that can be pushed wherever they sell. Having one inventory database also makes it easier to keep item details up to date, edit items in bulk, and organize inventory. This streamlined workflow reduces mistakes while making inventory much easier to manage. Advanced Reseller Analytics Growing a resale business requires more than increasing sales. It also requires understanding where those profits are coming from. Vendoo's analytics dashboard gives sellers a clearer picture of business performance by tracking important metrics across connected marketplaces. Instead of relying on estimates, sellers can review detailed reporting to understand which platforms generate the strongest results. Helpful insights include gross sales, net profit, ASP (average sale price), listing volume, and top-selling categories, sub-categories, and brands. These reports simplify bookkeeping while helping sellers decide where their time and inventory produce the greatest return. Flawless Sale Detection One of the biggest risks of crosslisting is accidentally selling the same one-of-a-kind item twice. Build a More Reliable Reselling Business with Poshmark Crosslisting Poshmark crosslisting is one of the most effective ways to grow a resale business without constantly sourcing more inventory . Instead of spending hours copying listings manually and tracking inventory with spreadsheets, use automation to streamline your workflow. Poshmark does not prohibit sellers from listing the same item on other marketplaces. Can I crosslist Poshmark listings for free? Yes. You can manually recreate each listing by downloading photos and copying your title and description into another marketplace. This costs nothing but becomes increasingly time consuming as your inventory grows. Which marketplaces work best with Poshmark crosslisting? title: Smurfit Westrock Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Smurfit Westrock Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
body_text: Smurfit Westrock plc (NYSE: SW) today announced the financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Key Points: Net Sales of $8,031 million Net Income of $88 million, with a Net Income Margin of 1.1% Adjusted EBITDA1 of $1,140 million, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin1 of 14.2% Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities of $765 million Quarterly dividend of $0.4523 per ordinary share Smurfit Westrock plc’s performance for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 (in millions, except margins and per share data): Tony Smurfit, President and CEO, commented: “I am pleased to report a strong second quarter performance with Adjusted EBITDA¹ of $1,140 million and an Adjusted EBITDA Margin¹ of 14.2%. The quarter was impacted by significantly higher input costs, particularly freight, which we managed to mitigate through our actions. Positively, demand for paper remained strong throughout the quarter with a generally excellent supply/demand backdrop. As always, we fully expect to recover input cost inflation through the second half of the year and beyond. “In the two years since the formation of Smurfit Westrock, we have driven a significant cultural and operational shift in our business. I have always believed that our strongest differentiators are the commitment and dedication of our people and the strength of our culture. As we target an accelerated path to growth through our Medium-Term Plan , I am excited that we have an excellent team which will realize Smurfit Westrock’s true potential. “Our North American region continues to make significant operational and commercial progress. Our team is progressively implementing our owner operator model and improving operating efficiency. Pricing initiatives have been implemented to recover increased input costs across practically all paper grades, and we are beginning to see the benefits from our commercial approach in our converting businesses. As we begin the third quarter, our mill system is generally running full with strong order books and an improving outlook for our converting operations. “Our EMEA and APAC region continues to outperform. This region is exceptionally well positioned and our actions on improving productivity and providing superior service and innovation for customers is gaining significant new business for us. While certain input costs are continuing to rise, these are being recovered with the customary lag. “Our Latin American region delivered another excellent performance as a result of our strong market positions and continuing benefits from our investment programs. We see significant growth opportunities, and we are well positioned to develop this region through both internal investment and acquisition. “In April we hosted over 200 global customers at our flagship innovation packaging event. I am very proud that we continue to be recognized by customers across all regions with numerous awards received for our approach towards innovation, sustainability and service. We continuously transfer best practice, operating excellence and innovation across markets, regions and continents for the benefit of our customers. “We also continued to optimize our system with a mill closure in the UK and are in the process of closing a further 8 facilities in our converting business in both Europe and the North American region. "Looking ahead, we are very encouraged by the current market back drop and the significant improvements we have made within our business. With input costs remaining elevated, especially freight, we currently expect third quarter Adjusted EBITDA2 to be approximately $1.3 billion and for the full year Adjusted EBITDA2 we expect to be in the range of $4.9 billion to $5.1 billion with good momentum through the latter half of 2026 and beyond. Download Q2 2026 Press Release Download Q2 2026 Presentation Dividend Smurfit Westrock plc announced today that its Board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.4523 per share on its ordinary shares. The quarterly dividend of $0.4523 per ordinary share is payable on September 10, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on August 14, 2026. Earnings Call Management will host an earnings conference call today at 7:30 AM ET / 12:30 PM BST to discuss Smurfit Westrock’s financial results. The conference call will be accessible through a live webcast. Interested investors and other individuals can access the webcast, earnings release, and earnings presentation via the Company’s website at www.smurfitwestrock.com. The webcast will be available at https://investors.smurfitwestrock.com/overview and a replay of the webcast will be available on the website shortly after the call.
